messages:
Jamie: Morning — quick async check for the rollout. Canary is currently at 3% (slice A). What I did: flipped feature flag to enable the new routing, kicked off canary, ran smoke tests. Observed a p95 bump on /v1/generate (~120ms -> ~220ms) after traffic started. Blockers: need to confirm whether this is batching-related or a model variant perf issue. Today: investigate KV cache miss rate and batching flags; request infra to check GPU utilization. Asking for a quick CR on #PR-4567 before any further ramp. Runbook hold: keep at 3% for 45m unless errors >1% or latency >350ms. Grafana: https://grafana.internal/d/abc123/canary-dashboard :eyes:

Sanjay: Saw the p95 bump as well, digging in. Reproduced a smaller version locally with the same request mix. Logs show the `batcher` on canary pods reporting `max_batch_size=1` which is suspicious. I'm patching the config to force batching back to expected values. If I can't fix in ~20m I'll roll back to previous variant. @Emma can you ping infra to check host-level GPU memory fragmentation/drivers?

Emma: On it. Opening an infra ticket and pinging eng-sre. I can also prepare a quick config patch: set `--max-batch=128` and `--batch-window-ms=12` for canary pods, and push it if you want. Need a fast CR from @Liam on #PR-4570 (tiny env flag change) before I apply.

Liam: Reviewing #PR-4570 now. One small docstring nit, otherwise LGTM. CI looks flaky on one test but not related. I can merge once the nit is addressed — should be <10m.

deploybot: Note: Canary auto-rollback policy in place. Conditions: >5% 5xx in a 10m window OR any OOM on canary nodes OR p95 > 400ms sustained for 5m triggers rollback. Autoprovision will also run healthchecks post-merge.

Jamie: Thanks. Important: do NOT increase canary % until p95 is back to baseline (or we have explicit sign-off). I'll update the runbook snippet and paste it here if helpful: ```# canary thresholds
ERROR_RATE_THRESHOLD=0.01
LATENCY_P95_THRESHOLD_MS=350
ROLLBACK_WINDOW_MINS=10
``` Keep manual hold until we confirm.

Sanjay: Pushing config now. Test command I used locally: ```kubectl set env deployment/infer-canary BATCH_SIZE=64 --namespace=staging``` After patching, I'll tail logs and post before/after p95 numbers.

Emma: Infra checked hosts — GPUs at ~62% mem, no OOMs. Host infra-07 shows elevated context-switches and a driver patch pending (ticket INF-1122). I'm coordinating with eng-sre to see if that maps to the noisy host. If needed we can drain infra-07 from canary pool.

Liam: CI fixed the tiny nit, merging now. Will post PR link when merged.

deploybot: Merge detected for #PR-4570. Initiating canary config rollout (3% -> 3% with new envs). If metrics remain stable for 10m, schedule automated bump 3% -> 5% in 10m. Autoclean/rollback watches enabled.

Jamie: Great. I'll be watching Grafana and the error dashboard. Plan to reconvene in 30m async standup with numbers. If anyone sees 5xx spikes or sustained p95 > 300ms, ping @Jamie and we'll consider immediate pause/rollback. :mag:

Sanjay: After the patch p95 dropped to ~135ms on the canary slice (first 5m). Posting short sample: baseline p95=120ms -> post-patch p95=135ms. No 5xx seen. Continuing to monitor and will post again at +15m.

Emma: Eng-sre responded — driver patch scheduled this afternoon, not blocking immediate canary, but will track. If behavior recurs correlate with infra-07. I'm standing by to remove infra-07 from rotation if needed.

Liam: Thanks all. Quick ask: if we end up rolling forward past 10%, can we gate by model variant instead of global ff? Might prefer staged by variant to limit blast radius. Happy to follow up in product sync.

Jamie: Noted. Let's keep that as a follow-up item. For now stay put at 3% until the 30m check. Thanks everyone for the quick turnaround.
